title: Human-like cross-language generalisation in deep neural speaker embeddings and its acoustic foundations
abstract: arXiv:2611.05384v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Generalisability is a central question for deep neural networks, including the cross-language generalisation of speaker embeddings. This study examined whether deep neural speaker embeddings generalise across languages and how such generalisation relates to human perception and acoustic structure. Using Cantonese--English bilingual speech presented in within- and cross-language conditions, we derived similarity from 18 state-of-the-art models and compared it with human ratings and acoustic features using linear mixed models and representational similarity analysis. Embeddings exhibited cross-language generalisation that broadly paralleled human behaviour, reflecting accurate identity discrimination and sensitivity to language switching. This generalisation relied on largely shared acoustic cues with language-sensitive weighting, mirroring human patterns. Together, these findings provide converging evidence for human--machine alignment in

translated_title: 深度神经网络说话人嵌入中类人的跨语言泛化及其声学基础
translated_abstract: 泛化能力是深度神经网络的核心问题之一，其中包括说话人嵌入的跨语言泛化。本研究考察了深度神经网络说话人嵌入能否跨语言泛化，以及这种泛化与人类感知和声学结构之间的关系。通过在语言内和跨语言条件下呈现粤语-英语双语语音，我们从18个最先进的模型中提取了相似度，并使用线性混合模型和表征相似性分析将其与人类评分和声学特征进行比较。结果表明，说话人嵌入表现出与人类行为大体一致的跨语言泛化，既能准确辨别说话人身份，又对语言切换表现出敏感性。这种泛化依赖于大体共享的声学线索以及语言敏感的加权方式，与人类的模式相呼应。总之，这些发现为人机在……方面的一致性提供了汇聚性证据。（注：原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 本研究证明深度神经网络说话人嵌入能像人类一样跨语言泛化说话人身份判断，其机制源于与人类相似的共享声学线索及语言敏感的加权策略。
en_tdlr: Deep neural speaker embeddings generalise across languages in a human-like manner, relying on largely shared acoustic cues with language-sensitive weighting that mirrors human perception.
